title: Cross-edge proxy refresh window accepts rotated API keys causing intermittent cross-org authorization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers running Dedicated and Private deployments reported brief windows where requests authenticated with a recently rotated API key were authorized against the old tenant mapping, resulting in reads/writes scoped to the wrong org. The issue occurred only during cross-edge proxy failover and during concurrent key-roll operations across control-plane and edge caches. Impact: intermittent cross-tenant access (read-only in most cases) for a subset of requests during rotation/failover. Affected environments: hosted (edge proxy path), Dedicated clusters configured with edge proxies, and Private VPC deployments using local edge cache replication. Scope: 3 enterprise customers reported escalations; internal smoke tests reproduced the behaviour at ~1-2% of rotation events in high-concurrency scenarios.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure two edge proxies A and B with cache replication (simulated network delay between them).
2) Start a high-concurrency workload (500 req/s) for customer org X using apikey v1 bound to org X.
3) Trigger key rotation: issue new apikey v2 and revoke v1 via control plane. Control plane publishes rotation event and updates tenant mapping.
4) Simultaneously failover edge proxy A -> B (simulate TCP reconnect/MS failover).
5) Observe that ~1-2% of requests carrying v1 are accepted and authorized under org Y mapping for a short window (10-30s) until caches reconcile.
root_cause: Race between control-plane rotation event and edge proxy cache reconciliation. When an edge proxy receives a revived session from another proxy that still accepts v1 (during failover), the local fast-path lookup uses an expired in-memory tenant mapping bypassing a fresh verification call. A combination of stale local TTLs, asymmetric eviction, and an optimization that avoids control-plane fetch during 'refresh window' allowed previously revoked keys to be accepted under wrong tenant bindings.
mitigation_taken: Hotfix (rolled at 2026-03-11): disable fast-path cache bypass on edges during key rotation windows; force control-plane verification for keys marked as rotated in last 60s.

Immediate customer mitigation: rotated keys for affected tenants and requested manual namespace rebind for any suspicious writes; rotated TLS certs on private deployments where customers requested extra assurance.
Monitoring: added temporary alert for any auth decisions where apikey_revoked=true AND tenant_binding_changed=true.
Communication: notified impacted customers and published incident notes in customer Slack channels and the enterprise incident tracker.
proposed_fix: 1) Make edge proxies consult the authority cache (control-plane) when a key has rotation metadata XOR when traffic comes from a different proxy than the one which initially issued the cached session. 2) Tighten TTL behavior: introduce adaptive TTLs for tenant mapping with aggressive invalidation during rotation events. 3) Add atomic update propagation for rotation markers across proxy fleet (gossip/commit log) to prevent asymmetric state.
implementation_notes: - Core change lives in gateway/auth/edge_cache.go: add a Hook verifyOnRotation(key) to force authoritative lookup.
- Add infra change to control-plane: publish rotation commit sequence numbers to the proxy commit log (controlplane/rotation_log service).
- Backwards-compatible: new proxies will accept commit-log header but legacy proxies will fallback to authoritative fetch; will introduce feature flag edge.auth.strict_rotation_check.
- Risk: small increase in control-plane calls during rotation bursts; mitigated by gating only keys with rotation metadata or cross-proxy origin.
testing_plan: Unit tests for edge cache hook and commit-log parsing.
Integration test harness that simulates dual-edge proxy failover and concurrent rotation at high QPS (repro script reproduced locally).
Staging rollout in us-west with synthetic tenants to validate risk <0.01% rotation acceptance after fix.
Canary rollout (10% of edge fleet) for 48h, then 50% for 24h before global.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR and run full CI (auth unit + integration). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6142
2) Deploy to staging, run integration harness for 6h.
3) Canary deploy to 10% of edge proxies (runtime-1.24-canary). Monitor alerts for auth_mismatch and controlplane_call_rate.
4) If canary is stable, promote to 50% then global over 12h.
5) Post-deploy run customer-specific replay tests provided in escalations.
